sources.citation: Wikipedia (zh), '水语', 音节结构 section (accessed 2026-09-17)
sources.note: Syllable template CjVCT and tone lists; no occurrence of 重音/轻音.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A., John H. Esling, Jimmy G. Harris & James Wei. 2004. A phonetic study of Sui consonants and vowels [Glottolog title: '..consonants and tones']. Mon-Khmer Studies 34: 47-66.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Instrumental study (tone plots, airflow, laryngoscopy) of Sandong Sui; §2 reviews Li 1948 / SDB 1956 / Zhang 1980 phonology (initials, 6 vowels, tones 1-8). The only 'stress' mentions (p.52) say the degree of stress and aspiration widens the glottal opening and lengthens VOT; nothing on where word stress falls.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en), 'Sui language', phonology section and reference list (accessed 2026-09-17)
sources.note: Vowels, tones, consonants, syllable structure only; no mention of stress. Reference list confirms Wei & Edmondson 2008 and Castro & Pan 2014 as the main descriptions.

sources.citation: Stanford, James N. 2014. Sui Adjective Modifiers. Linguistic Discovery 12(1). doi:10.1349/PS1.1537-0852.A.439
sources.note: A problem-set note on rhyming modifiers; no phonology sketch, no mention of stress.

sources.citation: Stanford, James N. 2007. Lexicon and Description of Sui Adjective Intensifiers. Linguistic Discovery 5(1). doi:10.1349/PS1.1537-0852.A.313
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §1.1 'Sui Phonology' gives a consonant table and the 10-category tone table for Ljaj Ku Tsong village (Zhonghe, Sandu); §1 says the language 'is isolating, tonal, and largely monosyllabic'. No mention of stress, accent or prominence anywhere in the article.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. & Kenneth J. Gregerson. 2001. Four languages of the Vietnam-China borderlands. In K.L. Adams & T.J. Hudak (eds), Papers from the Sixth Annual Meeting of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society 1996, 101-133. Tempe: Arizona State University.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §3 'The Thuy or Sui nationality of Vietnam': §3.1 Viet Sui tones (pitch plots, categories A/B/C/DL/DS mapped to tones 1-8), §3.2 initials compared with Sandong Sui. No statement on stress or accent.

sources.note: Sui has 13 WALS values, none for the stress features 14A-17A; WALS is silent.
